clue.text: Gasp! Crime everything one believes in?

parts.note: to gasp is to pant for breath
a heist is a robbery, a crime

explanation.surface: Someone gasps in shock at a crime that seems to embody all their convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: someone who sees God in everything could be said to believe in everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantheism identifies God with the whole universe, so its follower in a sense holds faith in all things.

clue.text: Finished with iodine, red mixture

parts.note: finished means over, past
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary, was a famous Red

explanation.surface: Done with the iodine, someone has a red mixture to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red mixture' looks like one phrase; red is the communist Che, and mixture is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a medley of borrowed styles or pieces, a hotchpotch.

clue.text: Upset queen doesn't want a republic

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top
doesn't want means the article is dropped from the word

parts.note: Regina is Latin for queen, used on coins and in titles

explanation.surface: An angry monarch rejects the idea of a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing A ('doesn't want') from REGINA leaves REGIN, which 'Upset' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked West African country that is a republic.

clue.text: Southern African, passionate figure, little one

parts.note: passionate means hot, fiery
ten is a figure, a number
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A passionate South African figure with a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is now considered offensive; it was an old name for the Khoikhoi people of southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Hottentot was a historical (now offensive) name for the Khoikhoi people of southern Africa.

clue.text: Picture puzzle with final twist I set up

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the letters are raised, read bottom to top
with final twist means the last two letters of the word swap places

parts.note: an enigma is a puzzle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A picture puzzle that I have arranged with a twist at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with final twist' swaps the end of ENIGMA to give ENIGAM; adding I and reversing all ('set up') gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to picture something in the mind.

clue.text: Tourist sees topless dancer

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter, its top in a down clue

parts.note: a stripper is a dancer who undresses

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker watches a dancer performing without a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' looks like a description of the dancer, but it removes the top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is a day tourist, a holidaymaker on a short excursion.

clue.text: Model question master?

definitions.meaning: a model is someone who poses for an artist or camera
a puzzling question that baffles, playfully called a master question

explanation.definitionFit: One who poses is a model; a tricky problem that defeats people is also called by this word.

clue.text: Snap end off tiny particle

indicators.note: end off means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a photon is a particle of light

explanation.surface: Someone breaks the end off a tiny particle.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is an informal word for a photograph.

clue.text: Shifting coastline in certain parts

indicators.note: shifting means the letters move around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A coastline that moves in some places.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectional means relating to or made of sections, existing in particular parts.

clue.text: Undesirable colour in shot, as programme finally in colour again?

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: to redye is to colour again

indicators.note: finally means take the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A TV programme's final scene, shot with unwanted colour, is re-coloured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from programme, and 'in' places it inside REDYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Red eye is the red glare in pupils in flash photographs, an unwanted effect.

clue.text: See something ugly

definitions.meaning: to see is to catch ... of

explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see it; informally, an eyesore or unkempt person is called this.

clue.text: During screening I return prisoner, securing a compound

indicators.note: screening means the first piece hides the others within it

parts.note: amid means during, in the middle of
taken as written

indicators.note: securing means the reversed prisoner holds the article inside it
return means the word for prisoner is read backwards

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: In a prison screening, an inmate who comes back is found holding a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' looks like a time link but is the container word; 'return' gives NOC and 'securing' makes NOAC before 'screening' wraps everything.
explanation.definitionFit: An amino acid is a chemical compound, the building block of proteins.

clue.text: Jewish prime minister short of leadership from Jerusalem?

indicators.note: short of leadership means losing the first letter, the one that leads

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli, the Victorian British prime minister, was born Jewish

explanation.surface: A Jewish premier is criticised for lacking guidance from the Israeli capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Disraeli was Britain's prime minister in the 1860s and 1870s.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Jerusalem is typically a citizen of Israel, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Integrity demonstrated by Ruth, squeezing Nick

indicators.note: squeezing means the first word holds the other tightly inside

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity or compassion
to nick is British slang for to steal, to rob

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth shows her honesty while hugging a man called Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth and Nick look like people's names; ruth is the archaic word for pity, and nick is slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Probity is uprightness and honesty, a straight synonym for moral soundness.

clue.text: Examination of feelings, when trying to conceal the scar, possibly

indicators.note: to conceal means the court word hides the other letters inside

parts.note: trying a case in court is hearing it

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of the words may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone does some soul-searching while trying to cover up a scar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' suggests attempting, but here it is the courtroom sense; 'possibly' makes TSEARCH and 'to conceal' hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart-searching is careful scrutiny of one's own emotions and motives, soul-searching.

clue.text: In harmony, people needing time for reparation

parts.note: at one means in agreement, in harmony
men are people

explanation.surface: People in agreement need time to make amends.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is making amends for a wrong, a form of reparation.

clue.text: Retreat sought from motorway cutting through estate

indicators.note: cutting through means the road goes inside the estate word

parts.note: heritage is an inherited estate
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A secluded spot is sought away from a motorway cutting through an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: M is used for British motorways (M1, M25).
explanation.definitionFit: A hermitage is a hermit's dwelling, a secluded retreat.

clue.text: Willingly taking exam, though most dim

parts.note: fain is an archaic word meaning gladly, willingly
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: Someone willingly takes an exam, though not the brightest.
explanation.definitionFit: Faintest is the superlative of faint, meaning least distinct or most dim.

clue.text: Order air assault to keep out explosive element in far off state

indicators.note: to keep means the rearranged letters hold the others within
order means put the letters of the following words into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
hydrogen, chemical symbol H, is explosive when mixed with air

explanation.surface: Commanders order an air raid to drive an explosive device out of a distant region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive' looks like the anagram signal, but 'Order' is; the rearranged letters, by 'to keep', surround the plain word and hydrogen's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: South Australia is a state of Australia, on the far side of the world from Britain.

clue.text: A sad diminishing love, with romantic feeling

indicators.note: diminishing means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: morose means sad, gloomy
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Fading sadness gives way to romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Amoroso is a musical direction meaning tenderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoroso is a musical term asking players to perform lovingly, tenderly.

clue.text: Headline writer does dirty plot in spades, say

indicators.note: in means the plot word goes inside the card word

parts.note: spades is an example of a suit of cards
a bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: A journalist digs a dirty plot with spades.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloggers queried 'dirty'; it seems to be read with 'does': a subeditor cutting a reporter's copy does the writer dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: A subeditor writes headlines and cuts copy, so this verb is what such a writer does.

clue.text: Old German coppers and shilling wanted in absence of change

parts.note: the Stasi were the East German secret police
S is the abbreviation for shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: Old German police and a shilling were wanted when nothing changed.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of equilibrium or inactivity where no change occurs.

clue.text: Another Etonian's confined to that place

indicators.note: confined means the letters are held within the run of the clue words

explanation.surface: A second public schoolboy is kept within the grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: An Etonian is a pupil of Eton, the English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereto is a formal word meaning to that thing or to that place.

clue.text: Guillotine almost too soon

indicators.note: to guillotine is to behead, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: A guillotine almost came too soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Early means before the expected time, too soon.

clue.text: Composer speaks of his home

indicators.note: speaks of means the word is said out loud and matched by sound

parts.note: the composer's home country is Britain

explanation.surface: A composer talks about where he lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Britten was a 20th-century English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten is a famous English composer, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Head of Tudor behind ruff ()

indicators.note: head of means take the first letter

parts.note: the behind is the rump

explanation.surface: A Tudor king's head is behind a ruff collar.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruff looks like the Tudor collar; in bridge to ruff is to play a trump card.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games, ruffing is playing a trump when unable to follow suit.

clue.text: Don's cutting blade which may be bloody

indicators.note: cutting means the clothing word slices into the blade

parts.note: a sword is a blade
to don clothes is to wear them; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A university don is wielding a blade that might end up bloodstained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like an academic, but it is the verb meaning put on; 'bloody' is the British swear word as well as gory.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain 'bloody' is a mild oath, so it is an example of profanity.

clue.text: Given poor treatment, one caught disease in the end

parts.note: a means one
something caught, like transport you catch, is a bus

indicators.note: in the end means take the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A patient badly treated has finally caught an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' is not cricket's C: you catch a bus. The definition fits only loosely, as 'given poor treatment' suggests the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Abuse means cruel or poor treatment, as when a person is mistreated.

clue.text: Stop to eat a Malaysian dish

indicators.note: to eat means the first word takes the other inside it

parts.note: to stay is to stop or remain

explanation.surface: Someone pauses to have a meal of Malaysian food.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is skewered grilled meat with peanut sauce, a dish from Malaysia and Indonesia.

clue.text: Where acne cream applied immediately

definitions.meaning: spot cream goes onto a pimple
right away, at once, without leaving the place

explanation.definitionFit: Acne cream is put directly onto a pimple; the idiom also means at once.
